claims.text: Article 29 of the SGG consolidated Law 31-08 text lists information for distance-sale offers, including essential product or service characteristics; supplier and, where applicable, responsible-offeror identification and contact details; delivery timing and cost where applicable; the right of withdrawal subject to exceptions; payment, delivery, or performance methods; offer validity and price; communication-technology costs; and minimum duration for continuous or periodic supply where applicable. It also says the offer information must be clear and understandable with its commercial nature unambiguous, and the supplier must present the consumer's choices before contracting and enable confirmation or modification of the order.
claims.pinpoint: Article 29, items 1–8 and final paragraphs; SGG consolidation dated 22 May 2025

claims.text: Article 30 of the SGG consolidated Law 31-08 text says a supplier must make the contractual terms for remote supply of products, goods, or services easily accessible and viewable on the supplier's website home page or another communication medium carrying the supplier's offer, and those terms must receive the consumer's express acceptance before the offer is accepted.

claims.text: Article 32 of the SGG consolidated Law 31-08 text says the consumer must receive, in writing or another durable medium at their disposal, in time and no later than delivery, confirmation of specified information under Articles 3, 5, and 29 unless already supplied before contracting; the supplier's complaint address; information on withdrawal conditions and process; after-sales service and commercial guarantees; and termination terms for indefinite contracts or contracts longer than one year. It also addresses no-extra-charge communications for tracking performance, withdrawal, or warranty, with a stated exception for one-off services delivered by distance technology and billed by that technology provider, except the supplier-address item.

claims.text: Article 33 of the SGG consolidated Law 31-08 text prohibits supplying products, goods, or services to a consumer without a prior order when payment is requested, says consumer silence is not acceptance, and says the consumer owes no payment for an unrequested supply.

claims.notes: Bounded English paraphrase of the Arabic consolidation, not an authoritative translation. claims.text: Article 34 of the SGG consolidated Law 31-08 text places the burden of proof on the supplier in a dispute, particularly for prior provision and confirmation of Article 29 information, observance of time limits, and consumer acceptance; it states that any contrary agreement is void and without effect.
claims.pinpoint: Article 34, paragraphs 1–2; SGG consolidation dated 22 May 2025

claims.text: Article 36 of the SGG consolidated Law 31-08 text provides a seven-full-day period to exercise withdrawal, extended to 30 days where the supplier fails to comply with the written-confirmation obligation for information under Articles 29 and 32. The provision says these periods run from receipt of the goods or, for services, acceptance of the offer. The surrounding provisions make this rule subject to Articles 38 and 42; it is not a universal withdrawal entitlement.
claims.pinpoint: Articles 36, 38, and 42; SGG consolidation dated 22 May 2025
claims.notes: Bounded English paraphrase of the Arabic consolidation, not an authoritative translation. The start point is paraphrased as stated in the provision: receipt of goods or acceptance of the offer for services. Article 42 excludes some contracts from Articles 29, 32, 36, and 37, while Article 38 lists exceptions to withdrawal. This claim does not enumerate or classify those categories or determine applicability. The SGG preface says the consolidation is for readability and Official Bulletin texts are authoritative; verify the Gazette text, amendments, and facts before applying it.

claims.text: Article 37 of the SGG consolidated Law 31-08 text says that when withdrawal is exercised, the supplier must refund the full amount paid immediately and no later than 15 days after exercise; after that period, the amount due accrues interest at the applicable legal rate.
claims.pinpoint: Article 37; subject to Articles 38 and 42; SGG consolidation dated 22 May 2025
claims.notes: Bounded English paraphrase of the Arabic consolidation, not an authoritative translation. Article 37 is subject to Articles 38 and 42, including listed withdrawal exceptions and excluded contract categories; this claim does not determine whether they apply in a particular case or calculate interest. The SGG preface says the consolidation is for readability and Official Bulletin texts are authoritative; verify the Gazette text and amendments before applying it.

claims.text: Article 38 of the SGG consolidated Law 31-08 text lists contracts for which withdrawal may not be exercised unless the parties agree otherwise: services begun with consumer consent before the seven-full-day period ends; supplies whose price or tariff depends on financial-market fluctuations; custom-made goods, goods that by nature cannot be returned, or goods liable to deteriorate or perish quickly; audio/video recordings or software once accessed by the consumer; and newspapers, periodicals, or magazines.
claims.pinpoint: Article 38, items 1–5; SGG consolidation dated 22 May 2025
claims.notes: Bounded English paraphrase of the Arabic consolidation, not an authoritative translation. The SGG preface says the consolidation is for readability and Official Bulletin texts are authoritative; verify Gazette text, amendments, and facts before applying it.

claims.text: Article 42 of the SGG consolidated Law 31-08 text says Articles 29, 32, 36, and 37 do not apply to contracts for regular doorstep delivery of ordinary consumer goods by distributors on frequent and regular rounds, or for accommodation, transport, restaurant, or leisure services to be provided on a specific date or during a specific period. It separately says Articles 29 and 32 still apply to electronic contracts for those listed services.
claims.pinpoint: Article 42, items 1–2 and final paragraph; SGG consolidation dated 22 May 2025

claims.text: Article 40 of the SGG consolidated Law 31-08 text says that if the supplier cannot perform the contract because the requested product, goods, or service is unavailable, the supplier must inform the consumer and, where applicable, refund amounts paid immediately and no later than 15 days after payment. After that deadline, the amounts accrue interest at the legal rate.
claims.pinpoint: Article 40; SGG consolidation dated 22 May 2025
claims.notes: Bounded English paraphrase of the Arabic consolidation, not an authoritative translation. claims.text: Article 41 of the SGG consolidated Law 31-08 text permits a supplier to provide a product, good, or service of the same quality and price if that option was disclosed before contracting or stated clearly and understandably in the contract. In that case, the supplier bears return costs arising from exercise of the withdrawal right and must inform the consumer of that allocation.

claims.text: Article 49 of the SGG consolidated Law 31-08 text gives a consumer up to seven days from the order or commitment to purchase to withdraw by sending the detachable contract form through any means that proves receipt. A contract term waiving this right is void and without effect. Article 49 does not apply to contracts concluded under Article 51.

The crossed-out old price may not exceed the lowest actual price the supplier charged at the same establishment for a similar item during the 30 days before the discount began. The supplier may also state the discount percentages.
